punchline: Hari's argument: apps built to hold your attention are doing their job, so the fix cannot be your willpower alone.
thirty_sec: In Stolen Focus, Johann Hari says apps are built to capture attention. He points to Facebook and YouTube as platforms that push screen time up to gather data and keep people engaged, and the book features Silicon Valley dissidents who learned how attention can be hacked. His answer is collective, from regulation to what he calls an attention rebellion.
